The study focuses on a two-bladed vertical axis wind turbine with a diameter of 1.7 m and NACA0015 airfoil-shaped blades.
The selected operating condition has a wind speed of 7 m/s and a tip speed ratio of 2.29, corresponding to an averaged Reynolds number of about 2.5x10^5.
The 2D computational domain is divided into four subdomains connected via non-conformal mesh interfaces, and the sliding mesh method is used to model the turbine rotation.
The baseline 2D mesh has 920,600 total elements with 1,000 nodes along each blade profile and a unity maximum y+ to resolve the boundary layer.
The sensitivity of the upstream torque coefficient to the domain size is less than 1% when going from the baseline to the extended domain.
The sensitivity of the upstream torque coefficient to the time step size is less than 1% when going from 360 to 1080 time steps per cycle.
The sensitivity of the upstream torque coefficient to mesh refinement is less than 1.1% when going from the baseline to a 3.1 times finer mesh.
The results based on the SST k-ω with γ model are generally more sensitive to mesh attributes compared to the SST k-ω model.
The 2D predictions of the SST k-ω with γ model show more deviation from the experimental data compared to the 3D predictions.
The paper highlights the need for detailed experimental data, such as pressure distributions, to properly assess the quality of CFD turbulence model predictions for VAWTs.
The study finds that the 2D results based on the SST k-ω with γ model deviate from the experimental data in ways that have not been previously investigated.
The use of the Coupled Scheme and Hybrid Initialization helps reduce the required number of cycles for a time-periodic solution compared to the SIMPLE Scheme.
The paper suggests that the 3D effects, such as tip losses, are important for accurate VAWT performance prediction, especially at higher tip speed ratios.
The study demonstrates the value of using detailed experimental data, beyond just the power coefficient, to critically evaluate CFD turbulence model performance for VAWTs.
The findings highlight the need for further research to improve the predictive capability of CFD models, especially for the SST k-ω with γ transition model, in 2D and 3D VAWT simulations.
